thread:
morgan: Quick q — I pushed a refactor that moves several provider blocks into our shared modules and updated module sources in terraform root. PR: https://git.company/repo/pull/482. CI plan is failing with provider version mismatch errors. Anyone seen this pattern?
kevin: Which error specifically? paste the plan snippet?
morgan: gist of error: 
```
Error: Provider configuration not present

  on .terraform/modules/db/main.tf line 2, in provider 
   2: provider 

The module "db" depends on provider registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws, but no provider configuration for that provider is present.
```
kevin: ah right — when modules define providers implicitly and we refactor to centralize provider blocks, you must either: 1) keep `providers = {}` mappings in module calls or 2) add an explicit `required_providers` + aliasing in root.
tara: Also check .terraform.lock.hcl — if modules were upgraded to a different provider plugin version, lockfile mismatch will cause CI to re-resolve and fail in some CI images. Did you update providers in any module?
morgan: I changed aws to ~> 4.60 in modules/db and modules/cache, but left root as ~> 4.51. I thought lockfile would pin it.
olivia: That explains it. Lockfile lives in the root workspace; if module fetch expects a newer provider binary but root lock pins an older one, terraform will try to update the lockfile during init which CI disallows by default.
infra-bot: :information_source: CI job `tf-plan` failed on branch refactor/module-providers — lockfile mismatch. See job logs at https://ci.company/job/482/34.
kevin: Options: update root `required_providers` to the higher constraint and regenerate .terraform.lock.hcl (locally or via CI job that allows updates), or align module constraints back to the root version. Also consider using `terraform providers lock` to pre-generate lockfile for supported platforms.
morgan: If we bump root to ~> 4.60 and regenerate lockfile, any state changes expected?
devops-sre: No state schema changes just from provider versions generally, but some provider upgrades do rename fields or change resource behavior. We should run a plan against staging workspace and scan diffs. Recommend: bump and run full plan in staging, not directly prod.
tara: Also watch for aliased providers. If some modules used provider aliases (e.g., aws.secondary) centralizing providers can break the mapping unless module calls include `providers = { aws = aws.secondary }` or similar. Search repo for `providers = {` before finalizing.
morgan: good call. I'll grep.
sam: Quick command to regenerate lockfile for CI across platforms: 
```bash
# from repo root
TF_REGISTRY_CLIENT_TIMEOUT=30 terraform init -upgrade -lockfile=write && terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64 -platform=darwin_arm64
```
kevin: ^ also ensure CI runner has same terraform version as dev machine. Lockfile encodes provider checksums; terraform version mismatches can influence provider plugin selection.
morgan: Who can review a small follow-up PR that bumps root required_providers and regenerates lockfile? I want to push before EOD deploy window.
olivia: I can review. Ping me when PR is up.
kevin: And add a note in the PR description: steps taken to validate (staging plan link, diff screenshots). Saves us a rollback. :+1:
morgan: will do. I plan to: 1) align required_providers in root, 2) run `terraform init -upgrade` locally and commit .terraform.lock.hcl, 3) push PR, 4) run staging apply after review. Any objections?
tara: No objections. Also add a short changelog in the repo's infra/README about the provider policy (pin at root, modules should avoid tight constraints unless necessary).
morgan: added to TODO. Thanks all — will post PR link here in a few mins.
infra-bot: :white_check_mark: New PR created by morgan: https://git.company/repo/pull/489 — bump aws provider to ~>4.60 and update lockfile. CI triggered.
kevin: I'll start the staging plan once CI passes.
olivia: Reviewing now.
morgan: CI failed on one platform checksum during providers lock step — investigating (looks like transient network). If it persists I'll try `terraform providers lock -platform` for fewer platforms to match CI matrix.
sam: If you need a quick helper, I can run the carriers check from my laptop and push the regenerated lockfile to your branch.
morgan: thanks sam, might take you up on that. will update thread. :wave:
